subject: Helix-3B tokenizer divergence — temporary version pin & routing ask
messages:
From: Kelly Ramos <kelly@atlasknow.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Trial request: Helix-3B (variant 'mx') — tokenizer note

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. Atlas Health is excited to try Helix-3B (variant label: helix-3b-mx) for our clinical summarization pipeline. Before we kick off a larger sandbox run we noticed a tokenizer/embedding delta between the model weights you provided and the tokenization scheme we currently use: some entity spans are split differently which causes subtle embedding drift for our retriever.

I've attached a small diff (tokenizer-diff.patch) and a ~200-record telemetry sample that reproduces the discrepancy. Can Redwood onboard helix-3b-mx for a short evaluation window and — if needed — pin traffic to a stable variant while we validate? Atlas would like a predictable routing behavior while we test.

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm whether the helix-3b-mx package uses a new tokenizer config by default?
- If so, can Redwood provide a pinned endpoint (helix-3b@v1.2) or a compatibility routing rule for our trial?

Appreciate any guidance.

—Kelly
Kelly Ramos
Platform Lead, Atlas Health

Priyom/Dev/Lauren, quick summary: Atlas Health sees a tokenization/embedding regression with helix-3b-mx vs their previous Helix baseline. They attached a patch and sample telemetry. Key asks: can we onboard helix-3b-mx for a short trial and either:

1) pin Atlas traffic to a stable build (they suggested helix-3b@v1.2) OR

Can you do a quick compat read and suggest the minimal operational change to keep Atlas' trial predictable? If pinning is required, please attach the telemetry summary and a proposed SLA exception form so I can get approvals.

Thanks — Ava

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trial request: Helix-3B (variant 'mx') — tokenizer note

Quick infra check completed — summary below.

Findings:
- The helix-3b-mx bundle we onboarded includes a tokenizer_config.json update that changes byte-pair merges for common clinical abbreviations (e.g., 'BP', 'ECG'). That causes token boundary shifts on ~6% of short clinical notes in Atlas' sample which explains embedding drift in their retriever.
- Model weights are fine; the mismatch is strictly tokenization.

Operational options (ranked by risk):
1) Temporary per-customer version pin: create helix-3b@v1.2 (old tokenizer) and route Atlas to that id for 7 days while they validate. Minimal infra work, low rollback risk.
2) On-the-fly tokenization shim: implement a compatibility layer that maps tokenization heuristics for Atlas' requests. Engineering effort: ~2 dev-days + runtime CPU overhead.
3) Global variant: change default tokenizer globally — NOT recommended without QA across customers.

Attachments: helix3b-telemetry-sample.csv (subset), tokenizer-diff.patch (patch showing token merges). Also created a short telemetry summary: helix3b-telemetry-summary.csv (attached).

Recommendation: option (1) — temporary customer pin to helix-3b@v1.2 for 7 days with automatic rollback to default after TTL. Devs can provision the pin and a scoped routing rule; I'll include a brief runbook for rollback. Need product approval + legal signoff if SLA is affected.

Runbook (high level):
- Create pinned model id: helix-3b@v1.2 (resource tag: "pin:atlas-ATL-4932")
- Add routing rule scoped by customer tag: route when request.header.x-customer-id == "ATL-4932"
- TTL: 7 days (configurable) + monitoring alert if error rate >1%
- Rollback: remove routing rule and untag resource.

I'll attach the telemetry snippet in case it helps approvals.

—Dev
Dev Patel
